observations.seen: Frames 1–3 have a low sun at the vanishing point and a warm golden glint on the asphalt, which matches the golden-hour recipe. Frame 4 shifts to a dark blue night sky, yet the player car is still lit bright orange, so the key light does not match the scene.

Traffic cars and the tow truck have only faint soft blobs under them, with no crisp cast shadows toward the camera from the low sun. The buildings cast no visible shadows onto the road, so vehicles look poorly grounded.

The player car has some glossy highlights on its blue body, but it reads as tinted plastic rather than lacquered paint. The road sun glint is a smeared hotspot, and in frame 2 its edge forms a blocky stair-stepped boundary near the truck.

The skyline is made of repetitive box towers with the same tiled window texture and no rooftop or facade variation. Overhead gantries ('SKYWAY 9 CENTRAL', 'EXIT 4B HARBOUR') add some context, but the world reads as procedural filler, and gold rings float oddly among the buildings.
There is mild haze at the far end of the highway and a soft sun disc. Distance fog is weak, though, and towers 100+ m away keep full contrast, so the 30–180 m fog depth layering is barely present.

The tow-truck ramp is a flat, untextured orange slab. Building textures are low-resolution and repeat visibly. Road asphalt detail is mostly destroyed by blur, while the traffic car materials (teal sedan, white van) are passable.
The player hypercar, sedan, van and truck models have reasonable silhouettes. The buildings are plain extruded boxes, and the tow-truck deck is a simple flat polygon.

Heavy radial motion blur smears the whole road surface into streaks, even at around 94 km/h. There is bloom on the sun and a warm grade, but frame 2 shows a pixelated stepped edge in the reflection/blur pass, and the overall look is smeary rather than cinematic film.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
